events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Green Mountains and Rattlesnake Range; East Sweetwater County
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Scattered snow showers ongoing across eastern Sweetwater County
into southern parts of Natrona County through mid Friday morning.
Up to 2 to 3 inches possible during this time, with greatest
concern for travel impacts for I-80 east of Rock Springs to
Wamsutter and Highway 287 from Jeffrey City to Muddy Gap. Be
prepared for rapidly changing road conditions overnight and into
the Friday morning commute due to slick roads and low
visibilities.

events.region: Northern High Plains; Eastern Glacier, Western Toole, and Central Pondera; Eastern Toole and Liberty; Hill County; Northern Blaine County; Southern High Plains; Eastern Pondera and Eastern Teton; Western and Central Chouteau County; Cascade County below 5000ft; Judith Basin County and Judith Gap
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
A mix of very low clouds and patchy dense fog continues across
portions of the plains this morning. Those with travel plans the
remainder of the night or early this morning should prepare for
widely varying visibility over short distances. If you encounter
fog slow down and use low beam headlights.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Ferris/Seminoe/Shirley Mountains; Central Carbon County; North Snowy Range Foothills; Southwest Carbon County; Sierra Madre Range; Upper North Platte River Basin
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Scattered snow shower activity is expected to continue across
Carbon County through Friday morning. Expect multiple rounds of
on-and-off snow showers accompanied by gusty winds. Be prepared
for rapidly changing road conditions and visibilities over short
distances. Slick, icy roads and visibility as low as one-quarter
mile will be possible under locally heavy snow showers.

Accumulations are expected to be hit-or-miss, with generally
between a dusting and 3 inches expected below 7500 ft in
elevation, and between 3 and 6 inches expected above 7500 ft in
elevation.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:

and waves 3 to 6 feet expected.

* WHERE...Grand Haven to Manistee.

* WHEN...From 3 PM this afternoon to 7 AM EST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

to be extended beyond Sunday morning. A cold front will move
through Sunday bringing breezy northwest winds and continuing
high waves into next week.

feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM EST Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
